outliers.video_title: ​6-Month Follow-Up After ACL Reconstruction & Meniscal Repair #shorts
outliers.channel_name: Dr. Yousef Muhammad | Knee & Shoulder Surgeon
outliers.why_it_worked: The '6-Month' timestamp gives viewers a concrete milestone to benchmark their own recovery against, reducing uncertainty about how long healing actually takes. The combination of two procedures (ACL + meniscal repair) signals complexity, making the follow-up feel high-stakes and credible. People in recovery are obsessed with 'where should I be at X months' and this title answers that question directly.
outliers.trend_or_evergreen: evergreen — ACL and meniscal injuries happen year-round and patients will always search for real-world recovery timelines regardless of when they find the video

outliers.video_title: Still experiencing shoulder pain after a previous surgery? There is hope for full recovery! #shorts
outliers.channel_name: Dr. Yousef Muhammad | Knee & Shoulder Surgeon
outliers.why_it_worked: The title directly addresses a painful, specific situation — someone who already tried surgery and still suffers — which filters for a highly frustrated, motivated audience. It validates their fear that they may never recover, then immediately counters it with 'there is hope for full recovery,' creating emotional relief and a reason to click. The combination of acknowledging past failure plus a credible medical source makes the promise feel trustworthy rather than hype.
outliers.trend_or_evergreen: evergreen — failed surgeries and persistent post-op pain are a permanent, recurring experience with no seasonal dependency
outliers.rewritten_title: Still Have Rotator Cuff Pain After Surgery? Here's Why — And How to Actually Heal
